family_id: PANTHER:PTHR24220
family_name: IMPORT ATP-BINDING PROTEIN
preferred_name: Type VII (ABC3-superfamily) ABC ATPase family including LolD, FtsE and HrtA
summary: >-
  PTHR24220 groups the nucleotide-binding (ATPase) subunits of a set of ABC
  systems whose membrane partners belong to the ABC-4/FtsX-MacB (type VII)
  superfamily. Reviewed members include the lipoprotein-release ATPase LolD
  (SF689, the largest reviewed subfamily), the cell-division ATPase FtsE (SF470),
  staphylococcal HrtA (SF666) and several uncharacterized or MacB-associated
  ATPases. All members are ABC ATPases, but the physiological outputs differ:
  LolCDE extracts lipoproteins from the inner membrane without moving them
  across it, and FtsEX regulates periplasmic cell-wall hydrolysis, so neither
  performs classical transmembrane substrate transport.
functional_coherence: HETEROGENEOUS
coherence_reason: >-
  ATP hydrolysis and association with the cytoplasmic face of the inner
  membrane are shared, but the coupled activities differ between subfamilies
  (lipoprotein release for LolD, cell-division signalling for FtsE, putative
  heme efflux for HrtA). Lol-pathway terms are safe only for the LolD
  subfamily, and transmembrane-transport terms are not safe for the LolD or
  FtsE subfamilies.

interpro/panther/PTHR30489/PTHR30489-rev.text:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR30489
family_name: LIPOPROTEIN-RELEASING SYSTEM TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN LOLE
preferred_name: LolC/LolE lipoprotein-release membrane subunit family
summary: >-
  PTHR30489 contains the integral-membrane subunits of the LolCDE
  lipoprotein-release complex of diderm bacteria. Members have four
  transmembrane segments and a large periplasmic domain of the FtsX/MacB
  (ABC-4) type. In E. coli the two paralogs are functionally differentiated:
  LolE binds the lipoprotein cargo and LolC recruits the periplasmic carrier
  LolA through its periplasmic Hook and Pad. Together with two LolD ATPases
  they release outer-membrane-destined lipoproteins to LolA without moving them
  across the membrane.
functional_coherence: COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  All reviewed members are LolC or LolE subunits of Lol release complexes, and
  the PAINT node for the family carries the Lol pathway and inner-membrane
  complex membership. The LolC/LolE role split is a within-complex
  specialization that does not change the complex activity the subunits
  contribute to.

document.summary: PTHR30489 contains the integral-membrane subunits of the LolCDE lipoprotein-release complex of diderm bacteria. Members have four transmembrane segments and a large periplasmic domain of the FtsX/MacB (ABC-4) type. In E. coli the two paralogs are functionally differentiated: LolE binds the lipoprotein cargo and LolC recruits the periplasmic carrier LolA through its periplasmic Hook and Pad. Together with two LolD ATPases they release outer-membrane-destined lipoproteins to LolA without moving them across the membrane.
document.coherence_reason: All reviewed members are LolC or LolE subunits of Lol release complexes, and the PAINT node for the family carries the Lol pathway and inner-membrane complex membership. The LolC/LolE role split is a within-complex specialization that does not change the complex activity the subunits contribute to.
